..(Sunday night through Friday)
Issued at 540 AM EDT SAT AUG 1 2026

The first part of the extended will be dealing with the de-
evolution of that too early synoptic low slowly working east 
through and eventually out of the eastern Ohio Valley. This will 
keep low clouds and some rain around well into the start of the 
new work week - continuing the heavy rain concerns - though a 
more diurnal pattern takes over with time for the convection.

The previous long term discussion follows:

The long-term period dawns Sunday morning with a weak, closed ~575
dam low spinning over southwest Indiana within a positively- 
tilted trough that extends northeastward toward James Bay, where a
broader 500 hPa trough is pivoting across eastern Canada. This 
upper-level low will lie nearly vertically stacked atop an 
occluding ~1004 mb surface low. While that does not sound all 
that impressive, the NAEFS and ECMWF ENS show that MSLP values of 
this depth fall below 1979-2009 CFSR climatology, indicative of 
how rare it is to have a developed mid-latitude cyclone passing 
through the Ohio Valley this time of year. The system's cold 
front will extend from the eastern side of the low near Cincinnati,
southward along the I-75 corridor into Tennessee, and then 
southward into the Lower Mississippi Valley.

While guidance still shows the northern stream 500 hPa trough
pivoting across Eastern Canada and adjacent portions of the  
Great Lakes and Northeast later Sunday and Sunday night and 
stealing some of the energy from the southern stream trough/ 
closing low, the 31/12z model suite seems to be latching onto more
of the vorticity energy remaining with the closed low and 
gyrating over the Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians on Monday 
and Tuesday. That system only slowly departs later in the week on 
Wednesday and Thursday as broad upper-level troughing develops 
over the North Central to Northeast CONUS, and an associated belt
of westerlies aloft captures the remnant low and sweeps it away. 
Flow over the Ohio Valley trends quasi-zonal by late week.

At the surface, the low pressure system over the lower Ohio Valley
remains nearly vertically stacked as it drifts to over the Mid-
Ohio Valley on Monday, where it wobbles and largely dissipates 
before its remnants are pulled away to the north by mid-week. As a
result, the system's cold front will slowly cross the JKL CWA 
during the day on Sunday. Within the warm sector, some of the 
longest-range CAMs are hinting at the possibility of enough shear 
and instability for at least weakly organized convection ahead of 
the cold front again on Sunday afternoon, especially closer to VA 
and WV. With the upper-level low lingering aloft, PWATs are now 
likely to stay elevated through the day on Sunday, as well as 
Monday and Tuesday (more so than what was expected in recent 
days). The result will be a lot more cloud cover and diurnally- 
modulated convection with greatest rainfall coverage during the 
afternoon and evening and continued though lower rain chances at 
night. The combination of a lingering nearly saturated deep warm 
cloud layer, skinny CAPE profiles, and elevated PWATs in the 1.75
to 2.00 inch range, warranted the addition of Marginal Risk EROs 
for both Monday and Tuesday. The threat for heavy rainfall 
subsides later in the week as the upper-level low departs and 
increasingly zonal flow allows drier and warmer air to filter 
eastward from the Plains mid-week. While a few pop-up 
thunderstorms will be possible from Thursday through Saturday, 
activity should remain more isolated to perhaps scattered and be 
confined largely to the afternoon and evening hours.

In sensible weather terms, look for a relative lull in the rainfall
Sunday morning, giving way to more widespread shower and thunderstorm
activity during the afternoon. Some of the convection could be strong
with gusty winds and torrential downpours. It will be humid and mild
with highs mainly in the lower 80s. Rain chances will then follow a
diurnal cycle on Monday and Tuesday, with coverage greater during the
afternoon and evening but still remaining possible at night. It will
be quite humid and muggy with afternoon highs mainly in the lower 80s
and nighttime lows in the mid to upper 60s. The pattern turns drier
from Wednesday onward with more sunshine and daily high temperatures
warming into the mid to perhaps upper 80s, while nighttime lows 
range from 65 to 70F.
